newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse lower, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse lower, seen consolidating.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings slightly lower on Monday, weighed down by a weaker dollar, with dealers saying the market was consolidating following the record-breaking run of recent weeks.

But the IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day dealings in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, received a late-afternoon boost when Wall Street surged ahead to touch new record highs. The IBIS DAX ended up 6.11 points, or 0.22 percent, at 2,733.67.

The DAX index had earlier closed floor trade down 5.79 points, or 0.21 percent, at 2,729.03 and had been unable to hold advances made in morning IBIS trade, which was boosted after data showed some slowing in German money supply growth.
In the morning IBIS had jumped to a new record of 2,745.82 points after the German central bank said money supply growth in September was an annualised 8.4 percent compared to 8.7 in August.

National telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom announced a price range of between 25 and 30 marks, in line with most forecasts, for the some 500 million shares in its initial public offering next month.

Dealers said Telekom shares were fetching between 37 and 39 marks in unofficial or so-called "grey trade". "We'd expect to be stable around these levels," said one trader. "We could go up or down 10 points, but not more than that."
The day's biggest loser in IBIS trade was German plant manufacturing group Duerr AG.
Duerr fell over eight percent to end down 4.50 marks at 50 marks after the firm said it expected 1996 profits to be lower than the 43.9 million earned in the previous year.
German airline Deutsche Lufthansa also slipped, ending computer trade three percent or 63 pfennigs down, at 20.35 marks. Dealers said high oil prices were weighing on the stock.
